extracted.intended_audience: Rospatent staff; patent attorneys; patent applicants; IP policymakers and stakeholders in the Russian Federation
extracted.subtask_description: Government annual report describing legal, procedural and performance standards for state registration, examination and administrative provision of intellectual property rights (patents, utility models, trademarks, industrial designs, appellations of origin, computer programs, databases, topographies) in the Russian Federation for 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirements for Geographical Indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indication: a sign identifying goods originating from the Region of a geographic area, where certain quality, reputation or other characteristics of such a product to a large extent should be associated with its geographical origin; in the Region at least one of the stages of production of the goods should be carried out, which has a significant impact on the formation of the characteristics of the goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The established requirements for legal protection of a geographical indication are softer than the requirements for the protection of appellations of origin (AOs). Geographical indications were introduced into Part IV of the Civil Code (Federal Law No. 230‑FZ, July 26, 2019). Use of GIs is expected to promote regional economies, tourism and preservation of traditional products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to attach three‑dimensional models and issue electronic certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft amendments provide the applicant the opportunity to attach three‑dimensional models of the claimed inventions, utility models, industrial designs, trademarks in electronic format to the application materials and propose issuance of electronic certificates on granted protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic certificates are allowed with the exception of patents for secret inventions; applicants may still request certificates on paper. These measures are part of the 'expansion of the use of electronic technologies in registering intellectual property rights' (Draft Federal Law No. 873108–7‑FZ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary information search and patentability evaluation by accredited organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Draft introduces the opportunity for Rospatent to create conditions for preliminary information search and evaluating patentability of the claimed technical solution by the Russian scientific and educational organizations accredited by Rospatent with competencies in specific areas of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation of such organizations will be free of charge. The preliminary information search service will be provided to applicants on a voluntary basis and is intended to improve examination procedures and the quality of incoming applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: State use/coercive measures for inventions in interests of national security and public health (Article 1360 amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft amendments to Article 1360 allow applying the legal mechanism for using an invention, utility model or industrial design in the interests of national security and in situations necessary to protect the life and health of citizens, with specification of guarantees for payment of compensation to patent holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology for determining the amount of compensation and the procedure for its payment will be approved by the Government of the Russian Federation. The Draft is stated to comply with Article 31 of the TRIPS Agreement (compulsory licensing/state use in emergencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative regulations: approval and modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Law 'On the organization of the provision of state and municipal services', administrative regulations are approved by the body providing the public services unless otherwise stipulated by federal laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rospatent prepared and submitted draft orders for public discussion to recognize previously adopted orders invalid and to draft new administrative regulations regulating provision of all 26 public services in its field, taking into account electronic provision of services and Geneva Act ratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control of workflow to improve quality of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures were strengthened to improve the quality of examination of applications for trademarks, including through internal control of workflow on applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthened internal controls are described as contributing to improved examination quality and reductions in average consideration time even when application volumes increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and expansion of electronic public services and automated systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of public services in electronic form and development of automated systems and electronic services are core tasks; in 2019 the number of requests submitted in electronic form increased by more than 40% relative to 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans include implementing 14 new information systems for registration and protection of IP rights by 2021, development of state patent collection and information services, and use of Rospatent internet resources and official publications to increase accessibility and convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicator: trademark examination time targets and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time of consideration of trademark applications in 2019: overall 5.96 months; national procedure 5.59 months (decreased by 2.07 months vs prior period); international procedure 6.33 months (decreased by 1 month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rospatent reports steady reduction of time limits for consideration of trademark applications and expects further reductions. Performance tracking includes numbers of applications examined, decisions on refusal/withdrawal/grant, and percent changes year‑on‑year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicator: invention (patent) examination time targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time limit of consideration of applications for an invention at the end of 2019 was 5.69 months (29.3% less than in 2018); average time limit of the first action of examination was 4.95 months in 2019 (versus 7.65 months in 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction of examination time is highlighted as enabling consideration of a greater number of applications. Rospatent publishes such timing metrics to monitor and manage examination capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicator: utility model examination time targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time limit of consideration of applications for a utility model in 2019 amounted to 1.35 months (52.8% less than in 2018); the average time limit of the first action was 1.11 months in 2019 (versus 2.64 months in 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short processing times for utility models are emphasized; branch contributions (e.g., Novosibirsk branch) to throughput are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicator: industrial design substantive examination time target
rubrics_metrics.description: The average time limit of consideration of applications for grant of a patent for an industrial design at the stage of substantive examination constitutes 4.4 months (2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rospatent notes this term provides a safety margin to meet government-established terms even in case of sharp increases in application receipts, including under the Geneva Act of the Hague Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary legal protection for industrial designs (publication‑based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary legal protection of industrial designs commences from the date of publication of information on the application for an industrial design, which is carried out at the request of the applicant after completion of formal examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This temporary protection is available upon applicant request; in 2019 Rospatent received no such applications. The mechanism is a procedural option applicants may use to obtain earlier provisional protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for authorized‑body conclusions in Appellations of Origin examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of applications for state registration of appellations of origin (AOs) and grant of exclusive rights is carried out on the basis of conclusions provided by federal executive bodies authorized by law to issue such conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rospatent cooperates closely with authorized bodies (notably the Ministry of Agriculture). Applications for goods lacking a defined authorized body continue to be received and may affect processing; obtaining conclusions is important to complete examination and grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated workflow for Geneva Act (Hague) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An automated workflow management system for applications filed in accordance with the Geneva Act of the Hague Agreement was put into operation in 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation supports handling of international (Geneva Act) filings and is part of broader digital modernization to support international registration systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and safeguards for electronic processes (secret inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic issuance of granted protection certificates is proposed broadly, with the exception of patents for secret inventions; paper certificates remain available at applicant request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secret (classified) inventions remain subject to special handling; digitalization applies where national security/classification rules allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with international obligations and bodies (WIPO, PCT, Madrid, Hague, TRIPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rospatent participates in WIPO, PCT, Madrid, Hague, EPO, EUIPO, CIS, EAPO, EAEU, BRICS, WTO and bilateral cooperation; it fulfills international obligations and promotes Russian language use in international registration systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cites leadership in WIPO task forces (3D, blockchain), participation in Patent Prosecution Highway, and work to update international IP standards — indicating that domestic procedures are framed to be consistent with international instruments and cooperation programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and registry management (amendments, renewals, cessations, restorations, open licenses, court decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: State registers are subject to amendments, renewal, cessation, restoration of legal protection of IP objects; Rospatent publishes open licenses and court decisions and provides for registry maintenance actions as procedural steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updating and publishing registries and court decisions are part of administrative services; Rospatent planned changes to administrative regulations to account for electronic provision and registry management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation and training as support for examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Rospatent accredits scientific and educational organizations, runs training programs (advanced professional training, professional retraining), and provides methodological support (e.g., methodological basis of patent research, criteria for IP protection eligibility) to improve examination and patent research competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation is free; numerous educational programs, seminars and corporate events are listed to develop examiner and stakeholder competencies in patent search, preparation and examination by sector, and patent analytics.
